items.title: Minimum Requirements
items.text: • Dart SDK: ^3.8.0

items.title: 1. Detect your architecture
items.text:
Read your pubspec.yaml to extract the app name and SDK constraint, then scan the lib/ directory to identify your project’s architecture pattern:

Signal Likely pattern lib/ has data/, domain/, presentation/ Clean Architecture lib/ has data/, domain/, ui/ or views/ Clean Architecture (variant) Files named *viewmodel.dart, *screen.dart MVVM Files named *_cubit.dart, *_state.dart BLoC / Cubit Files named *_controller.dart GetX or Controller-based Files named *_provider.dart, *_notifier.dart Provider / Riverpod Directories named by feature (e.g. auth/, home/) Feature-based lib/ has models/, repositories/, services/, utils/ Layer-based

items.title: 2. Create eagle_eye_config.json
items.text: Create this file at the project root (same directory as pubspec.yaml). It is a JSON array of rule objects.

items.title: Rule types
items.text: Key Type Effect filePattern string Wildcard pattern matching file paths. * becomes .* regex. dependenciesAllowed boolean If false, matched files must have zero internal imports. forbiddenDependencies string[] Matched files must not import anything matching these patterns. exclusiveDependencies string[] Matched files can only import things matching these patterns. name string Optional human-readable name (shown in violation output).

items.title: Architecture-specific templates
items.text: Pick and adapt the template that matches your architecture.

items.title: Clean Architecture (data/, domain/, presentation/)
items.text:
[
  {
    "filePattern": "*/domain/model/*",
    "dependenciesAllowed": false,
    "name": "domain-models-no-imports"
  },
  {
    "filePattern": "*/domain/*_repository.dart",
    "exclusiveDependencies": ["*/data/*"],
    "name": "repositories-only-data"
  },
  {
    "filePattern": "*/presentation/*",
    "forbiddenDependencies": ["*/data/*"],
    "name": "presentation-no-data"
  }
]

items.title: MVVM (*viewmodel.dart, *screen.dart)
items.text:
[
  {
    "filePattern": "*viewmodel.dart",
    "forbiddenDependencies": ["*_screen.dart"],
    "name": "viewmodels-no-screens"
  },
  {
    "filePattern": "*screen.dart",
    "exclusiveDependencies": ["*_viewmodel.dart", "*_widget.dart"],
    "name": "screens-only-widgets-and-viewmodels"
  }
]

items.title: Feature-based (directories named by feature)
items.text:
[
  {
    "filePattern": "*/features/*/data/*",
    "exclusiveDependencies": ["*/features/*/domain/*"],
    "name": "feature-data-depends-on-domain"
  },
  {
    "filePattern": "*/features/*/domain/*",
    "dependenciesAllowed": false,
    "name": "feature-domain-no-imports"
  }
]

items.title: Generic / starter config
items.text:
If the architecture is unclear or doesn’t match a specific pattern, use this conservative starter:

[
  {
    "filePattern": "*/model/*",
    "dependenciesAllowed": false,
    "name": "models-no-imports"
  },
  {
    "filePattern": "*/data/*_repository.dart",
    "exclusiveDependencies": ["*_datasource.dart"],
    "name": "repositories-only-datasources"
  }
]

items.title: Customization guidelines
items.text:
• Start with a small set of rules (2-4). You can add more as your architecture stabilizes.
  • filePattern matches against the full file path relative to lib/. Use * as a wildcard.
  • Rules are evaluated in order; first matching rule wins for each file.
  • Only internal imports (those containing your app name) are checked. External package imports are ignored.
  • Each rule object should have at most one of: dependenciesAllowed, forbiddenDependencies, or exclusiveDependencies.

items.title: 3. Configure analysis_options.yaml
items.text:
Eagle Eye requires package-style imports (not relative imports). Ensure this lint rule is set to error.

If the file does not exist, create it:

analyzer:
    errors:
        avoid_relative_lib_imports: error

If the file already exists, add or merge the errors section:

analyzer:
    errors:
        avoid_relative_lib_imports: error
        # ... other existing error rules

This enforces imports like:

// GOOD - package import
import 'package:my_app/utils/helper.dart';

// BAD - relative import
import '../utils/helper.dart';

items.title: 4. Add Eagle Eye dependency
items.text:
Add to pubspec.yaml under dev_dependencies:

dev_dependencies:
    # ... existing dev dependencies
    eagle_eye: ^2.0.4

Then run:

dart pub get

Or for Flutter projects:

flutter pub get

items.title: 5. Validate the setup
items.text:
Run the CLI:

dart run eagle_eye:main
  • Exit code 0 with a success message: setup is correct.
  • Exit code 1 with violations listed: the rules are working — review the violations to confirm they are real issues or adjust your config.

items.title: 6. Optional — integrate into CI/CD
items.text:
Add to your CI pipeline (e.g. GitHub Actions, GitLab CI):

- name: Check architecture rules
  run: dart run eagle_eye:main

Eagle Eye exits with code 1 on violations, so the CI step will fail automatically if architecture rules are broken.

items.text:

After completing all steps, run dart run eagle_eye:main to confirm everything works.

items.title: AI-assisted setup
items.text:
You can use this prompt with an AI assistant to automatically detect your project’s architecture and generate an appropriate eagle_eye_config.json.

Any problems you are facing, any suggestions you want to add, please feel free to reach us out.

items.title: Existing rules 📐
items.text: We have several rules already defined in the plugin. You can create some rule too, take a look in our section about contributions.

items.title: Forbidden Dependencies Rule
items.text:
Deprecated - Only available before v2.0.0

The DoNotWithRule specifies that a set of file should not depend on certain files. For example:

// your-project-root/eagle_eye_config.json
{
  "filePattern": "*viewmodel.dart",
  "doNotWithPatterns": ["*_screen.dart"]
},

The Forbidden Dependencies Rule specifies that a set of file should not depend on certain files. For example:

// your-project-root/eagle_eye_config.json
{
  "filePattern": "*viewmodel.dart",
  "forbiddenDependencies": ["*_screen.dart"]
},

In this case, all files that has the suffix viewmodel.dart should not depend on any file whose name includes ‘_screen.dart’.

items.title: Exclusive Dependencies Rule
items.text:
Deprecated - Only available before v2.0.0

The JustWithRule specifies that some files should depend on certain files. For example:

// your-project-root/eagle_eye_config.json
{
  "filePattern": "*repository.dart",
  "justWithPatterns": ["*_datasources.dart"]
},

The Exclusive Dependencies Rule specifies that some files should depend only on certain files. For example:

// your-project-root/eagle_eye_config.json
{
  "filePattern": "*repository.dart",
  "exclusiveDependencies": ["*_datasources.dart"]
},

In this case, the our repositories should depend only on data sources.

items.title: Dependencies Allowed Rule
items.text:
Deprecated - Only available before v2.0.0

The NoDependencyRule ensures that some files should remain free of any dependencies. For example:

  {
    "filePattern": "*util.dart",
    "noDependsEnabled": true
  },

The Dependencies Allowed Rule ensures that some files should remain free of any dependencies. For example:

  {
    "filePattern": "*util.dart",
    "dependenciesAllowed": false
  },

In this case, the all utils should be free of any internal dependencies.

items.title: Contributions 🤝
items.text:
We encourage contributions of all types! Whether it’s reporting issues, suggesting new features, or submitting pull requests, you’re welcome to help improve the plugin.

  • Check out the issues page for ideas.

  • Feel free to submit pull requests.

items.title: 1. Fork the repository
items.text: Create a fork of the repository in your own GitHub account.

items.title: 2. Clone the repository
items.text: git clone https://github.com/your-user/your-fork

items.title: 3. Access the repository
items.text: cd your-fork

items.title: 4. Make your changes
items.text: • Update the code.

items.title: 5. Commit the changes to your fork
items.text:
git checkout -b "your-branch-name"
git add .
git commit -m "Describe your changes"
git push

items.title: 6. Create your Pull Request
items.text:
• Create a new Pull Request, selecting the original repository as the base and your branch as the compare branch

  • Provide a clear title and a detailed description of your changes

  • Submit the PR and wait for review and possible approval.

🤗 Happy coding!

items.title: How to run the docs locally?
items.text:
• Create your virtual env:
python3 -m venv venv
  • Open the new env:
source venv/bin/activate
  • Install Zensical (pinned version):
pip install zensical==0.0.46
  • Start the local server:
zensical serve

Access your documentation at http://127.0.0.1:8000/

Zensical is in active development — the version is pinned to avoid breakage. Bump manually when needed.
